<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/spec-changes.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6ceddc3c4deb9d56025fff9fae03d65b62e95a7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c91e0979bb5e5fdc4196e442ae103cce0a7fef61` — the merge of head `fee9df53f7f3d2cd64ff5fa7b1d079aff350f719` into base `f6ceddc3c4deb9d56025fff9fae03d65b62e95a7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c91e0979bb5e5fdc4196e442ae103cce0a7fef61 && git checkout c91e0979bb5e5fdc4196e442ae103cce0a7fef61
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f6ceddc3c4deb9d56025fff9fae03d65b62e95a7 fee9df53f7f3d2cd64ff5fa7b1d079aff350f719 && git checkout -B drift-repro f6ceddc3c4deb9d56025fff9fae03d65b62e95a7 && git merge --no-ff fee9df53f7f3d2cd64ff5fa7b1d079aff350f719

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6ceddc3c4deb9d56025fff9fae03d65b62e95a7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fee9df53f7f3d2cd64ff5fa7b1d079aff350f719`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20233 (body + all 27 comments, incl. rulings and the stage-1…7 records), PR #20568 body, its 33-file list and the net diff `origin/main...fee9df53f7` (merge-base `288611e3`), the 46 check-runs on the head, ruling C+D `5749154545` on #19123, ruling A `5858839916`, and — to check rewritten sentences — the cited cards and threads by REST plus `git show` of `main`'s commits and CHANGELOGs. Nothing built, run or re-run; the only local operation beyond reads was a three-way `git merge-file` of `registry.ts` written into scratch (see ③).

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — nothing moves (right).** I mapped every changed line of the 28 entry files, on both sides of every hunk, to its enclosing object key: only `reason`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are touched. No `id`, `surface`, `from` / `to`, conversion, matcher, import or comment token changes; every removed `ADR-NNNN` token is present on an added line (ADR-0033 / 0049 / 0058 Amendment II.2 / 0078 / 0087 / 0090 D3 / 0104 all kept). The three generated projections change only text: `registry.ts` +195/−126 — the entry files' own +195/−126; `spec-changes.json` 16 `rationale` + 4 `replacement` fields (the sixteen protocol-17 entries whose `reason` changed and the four whose `replacement` changed; protocol-18 entries do not project until that major ships); `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` 25/25 lines. Tracker ids on added lines across all four: 0. `check:migration-registry` (Lint & Repo Gates) and `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` (Type Check · source gates) are success on the head. `Clause-②: no` is the right reading.

**Public surface — the printed guidance changes, as intended (right).** The surface that moves is the text `os migrate meta` prints for 28 semantic entries. 73 distinct `#N` tokens leave the prose (63 objectstack ids, `objectstack#6739`, five objectui ids, `cloud#1203`, `duly#109`, and the two decision-batch numbers #119 / #121); 0 remain on added lines; a scan of the non-comment lines of all 30 entries under the fourteen prefixes at head finds no `#NN…` at all, including the three untouched entries (`dashboard-refresh-interval-unit-in-key`, `record-highlights-field-icon-retired`, `rls-check-on-select-or-delete-policy-refused`). Comment lines are untouched (#20234's carrier).

**Form D — each rewrite says what its source decided.** Sampled against sources, weighting the dead and unreadable ids:
- 404s (6 by my probe: 6048, 6148, 6361, 6363, 11693, 11757). `#6048` → `main` `dca5bd36af`: maintainer ruled 2026-08-06 immediate retirement, no window, no dual-emit; the pins were flipped in the same batch — matches "the pins the removal flipped". `#6148` → `main` `81a4a670b1`: the ADR-0087 ledger-completeness gate, "a changeset declared breaking must state its ledger disposition" — matches the rewrite verbatim in sense (apimethod-, record-, runtime-). `#6363` → `main` `17d0954132` + spec CHANGELOG: `listInbox`'s `unreadCount` counts the whole inbox, ruled jointly 2026-08-07 Option A — matches. `#6361` → `90bbf25107`, the entry's own retirement: dropped, nothing to say. `#11693` / `#11757` → platform-objects CHANGELOG (`4d25d22`): ruling 2026-08-24 「不需要考虑历史数据」, reaffirmed 2026-08-25, no data migration, retired after the 1.7.1 migration landed — the shortened quote keeps exactly the words the CHANGELOG records.
- 403s. `cloud#1203` → #6781 body: "maintainer ruling 2026-08-08: option B … restore it upstream, correctly shaped" vs A "cloud hand-rolls S3 pagination — recreates the retired defect one repo over" — the storage- acceptance sentence is exact. `duly#109` → objectui#7293 body: "building a manager dashboard in duly … a KPI tile for a rate plus a two-number sub-caption" — matches "the wish, from a downstream application's manager dashboard, for several numbers on one tile".
- Dated rulings and letters, each read in its thread: #6011 14:49:30Z 「roles 别名现在就关闭」; #5574 "forbids silently picking re-resolution" (quote present); #6752 2026-08-09 route 2; #7990 Option A adopted 2026-08-12, class-level guard parked, reopen trigger "a third measured artefact-type surface", the two measured surfaces being driver config and connector `authentication` (#8075 body); #8075 fork (b) = unreachable from any `sys_metadata` door; #5552 2026-08-06 B, and `main`'s `shared/FieldMapping:transform` tombstone itself says "the whole `FieldMappingTransform` union went with it … no runtime ever executed any of the five"; #11825 2026-08-25 route 2 (retire the container, classes stay a host-driven library); #6739 2026-08-09 A; #17385 2026-09-12 C+D (batch 121 item 1); objectui#8894 2026-09-12 D (batch 119 item 4) under 「协议不正确的应该先修改协议」; #8762 2026-08-15; #5266 2026-08-05 option 2; #19886 ruling A 2026-09-24 "refuses an array under `$ne` for every driver", and its 2d list item (c) is the ordering operator against an array comparand — so the stored-list-ordering sentence ("the mirror … of the earlier refusal of an ordering operator against an array comparand, one of the same-class leaks") is what the thread says; #19757 ruling 乙 2026-09-23 "for every driver at once"; #5222 review: `{ stage: { $gt: { $field: 'amount' } } }` returns four rows on SQLite (TEXT above INTEGER) and none in memory, hence the same-class operand rule — the cross-class sentence is exact; #3653 body: `{ fields: ['provider_id'], unique: true }` against upstream's organization-scoped `provider_id` boundary, recorded while parked on rc.1 — the scim- sentence is exact.
- Measurements and fixes by title/body: #5050 (zero producers, zero consumers), #5697 (declared as-is, first stage of the contract-first ruling on #5613), #4484 (no caller), #5540 (zero consumers), #3950 ("None of it was ever wired to anything"), #3733 (parses successfully, key silently dropped, non-strict schema), #7532 (dotted nonexistent column answers 200 + every field), #6924 (hint prescribed an unmaterialisable formula/rollup denormalisation), #5272 (single-row delete never bound `previous`), #6697 (before* hooks per matched row on a bulk write), #16320 (`DataSyncConfig.schedule` is one of the seven cron-typed positions), #4738 (automation copy dead-deleted), #4962 (third retry vocabulary #4661's convergence missed), #2377 (`trash` among the dead `enable.*` flags, 11.0 ADR-0049), #6350 (227 v17-train breaking changesets never compared), #3543 = P2 (phase 2) of #3391, #5011 (three arms dead: two silent, one throwing), #17344 §1 "Honoured by the funnel branch only", #3899 / #4052 / #4666 / #5611 / #5122 / #20347 / #20355 (titles state the lesson written), #12726 (stable 1.7.1 as one whole-model migration, #3653's own framing).
- Carry-over: #13823 is "filed out-of-scope from the published-skills factual sweep, flight ⑦ (`skills/objectstack-api`)"; #13808 is flight 6 (`skills/objectstack-automation`). "a factual sweep of the API skill" is now right.

**Wording notes, none a FAIL item** (no decision invented, overstated or changed; no number returns): (i) runtime-httpserver: "since publish stopped refusing them" — #5111 narrowed publish's blanket refusal to per-endpoint gating (unsupported subset + namespace gate); the sentence's lesson (from 17 on, `setFallbackHandler` is the only entry path because declarative endpoints execute) stands. (ii) etl: "the `activationEvents`, dynamic plugin-loading and widget / i18n retirements each let an earlier tombstone go" — the activationEvents entry on `main` records its own tombstone going with `DynamicLoadRequest` under the plugin-runtime removal; the pattern each entry records is the one named, the actor is grouped loosely, as the base's "#4657/#4834/#5055 way" already grouped it. (iii) storage: "the email plugin's large-attachment storage work" — #5172 is the attachments-through-storage-references card; "large" is a gloss on its size-driven reasoning.

**Would a reader of `os migrate meta` now be misled?** No. Every dropped id is replaced by a clause resolvable inside the printed block (header + `why:` + `verify:`): e.g. hot-reload-inert's `verify:` "That ruling's keep itself stands" points at the 2026-08-25 ruling its own `why:` names; notification's "(it was the jointly ruled repair's business)" points at the repair its `why:` describes; rls-cross-class's "the earlier refusal of an array comparand under `$ne`" names the sibling entry's refusal. No dangling antecedent found across the 28 blocks, and no sentence now states a decision its source did not take.

**Pin (right).** `COVERED_PREFIXES` gains exactly the fourteen prefixes the PR body names (41 total; every prefix selects at least one entry — 30 under the fourteen). `REWRITTEN` 147 → 174: the 27 added rows are the 27 entry files under the fourteen prefixes the diff touched (26 with four/five-digit sites plus `dashboard-widget-chart-config-structure-refused`, which carried only a decision-batch number); `rest-api-endpoint-handler-status-retired` was already a row. Assertions and detector unchanged. The file is queue-population by name (not `.e2e`/`.live`), so it ran in Test Core (`turbo run test test:repo`), 6/6 shards success.

**PR body, sentence by sentence — true of the diff.** `Part of #20233`, no closing keyword (gate "Part-of PR must not also close its card": success). The stage line's fourteen families = the fourteen prefixes added. `Clause-②: no` stands alone. "Text only … ADR ids stay. No entry `id`, `from` / `to`, conversion or matcher changes" — proved above. Carry-over sentence — true (#13823 provenance). Pin sentence (`COVERED_PREFIXES` + fourteen, floor 174) — true. "regenerated" — the equality gates are success. "`patch` changeset" — `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. The report id `5883241063` is the stage-7 dev report on the card. The changeset body's claims (no `surface` changes; the chain rewrites exactly what it rewrote before) hold: no `surface` line and no conversion is touched.

Report-count notes, immaterial and not in the PR body: the dev report says seven cited ids answer 404; my probe of every removed id reads six. It says 63 objectstack ids; the removed lines carry 64 including `objectstack#6739`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch** — right. The published package's content changes (the entry prose is runtime data: `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` is imported by the CLI and printed), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; no type, schema, accept set, conversion or export moves, so nothing above patch is owed. `packages/cli` changes a test only — no changeset owed. Check Changeset: success (both runs). `Clause-②: no` — right: no accept set moves, on my own key-lookup of every changed line.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (the report's `deviations`; `open_questions` is empty):
1. Deletion leg run after the rewrite, from committed HEAD — answered: acceptable for a text-only change; the six reds are the readers of these fields and every asserted fragment survives; the pin's own ablation (query-cursor-retired `reason` reverted → "expected '#4286' to be undefined" red → restored green) is the anti-vacuity proof. Not re-run here.
2. Census and astdiff scripts rewritten in-container — answered: my independent line-and-key probe (28 files, three prose keys only, 0 non-prose lines, 0 comment lines) reproduces the text-only claim without them.
3. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally, declared to CI — answered: Build Core hosts it ("Every published require entry point actually loads" → `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) and is success on the head.
4. `/del.pid` written at the container's filesystem root — outside the repository and the diff; nothing in the PR carries it. Noted for a person; not a contract matter.
5. Floor arithmetic (27) — verified: 147 → 174, and the 27 rows are the 27 touched files (above).
6. Attribution — both branch commits carry the session-URL trailer and the model-free co-author line; the PR body ends with the session-URL footer. Not a contract matter.
7. `origin/main` not merged — `main` has since moved to `1c761c0d71`; of the PR's 33 paths only `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` moved (`ba5927f714`, PR #20460, adds `stack-config-default-export-unbuilt-refused`).
